chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his father, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, who said: Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakoony, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: 'The gift is a good thing before the need arises,' and he said: 'Exchange gifts so that you may love one another, for the gift removes animosities.'

key_terms.تَحَابُّوا: Love one another / Foster mutual love

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social benefit of giving gifts in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizing that proactive gift-giving serves as a strategic means to preemptively dissolve animosity and cultivate mutual affection. This tradition highlights the social utility of gifts in Shia ethics, not merely as charity but as a tool for maintaining communal harmony and erasing lingering grudges. The teaching aligns with the broader Islamic principle that material generosity strengthens spiritual bonds and fosters a culture of love among believers.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-97 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Sahl ibn Zyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Abi Zyad al-Sakoony that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,
“Giving a gift before asking for something is good. Exchange gifts and be friends since giving gifts will eliminate animosities.”
